title: Insane 2-Bit AI Compression: Run a 27B Model on an 8GB Laptop!

raw_text: Honestly, this is huge news for anyone who loves running local AI on their own machine! The open-source community just dropped Underdog Saluki 27B, and it pulls off an absolute miracle of edge compression. They took a massive 27-billion-parameter model that normally eats fifty-four gigabytes of high-end VRAM and crushed it down into a tiny seven-point-eight-nine gigabyte file! How? By using targeted two-bit ridge quantization. Historically, dropping precision that low scrambles a model's brain, ruining JSON output and API calls. But here is the wild part: Saluki 27B actually scored higher on a 120-task tool-calling benchmark than the uncompressed original model, scoring eighty-eight versus eighty-four! That changes personal computing forever, and I am definitely installing this today!
